question: For a Wireless Communication use case involving Wi-Fi 7/8, where would Signaling / Non-signaling Tester fit in the test workflow?
answer: In the Vault, the signaling and non-signaling testers cover two different stages of the Wi-Fi 7/8 workflow. In R&D, the R&S CMX500 is the multi-technology, multi-channel signaling tester. It measures RF TX/RX characteristics in signaling mode under real-world conditions and covers MLO with multiple RF chains, 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz band with out-of-band discovery, coexistence and E2E tests. It also covers 5G/WLAN offloading and Voice over WLAN using its N3IWF gateway and POLQA. In production, all WLAN RF measurements run in non-signaling mode to save time, and the R&S CMP180 non-signaling tester does this work. It supports Wi-Fi 6E, Wi-Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz, and two units can be combined to test 4x4 MIMO access points. For Wi-Fi 8, the CMX500 ran the first Wi-Fi 8 RF tests in signaling mode on a prototype Broadcom device, including dRU and UEQM. The CMP180 showed a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode, which the source calls only a potential Wi-Fi 8 waveform candidate.
missing: The evidence is PR/demo material only. It gives no option codes, software versions, RF chain counts, test case lists or measurement uncertainty for Wi-Fi 7/8 on the CMX500 or CMP180. It does not name the IEEE 802.11bn draft version, says nothing about a Wi-Fi 8 production (non-signaling) workflow beyond the 480 MHz loopback demo, and does not describe certification or test-house steps.
